title: Value > Suffering Reframe
opening: A project can matter while one of its operations adds nothing useful. Examine each difficult part on its own.

labels.exampleContext: A team wants learners to understand a procedure. They verify the demonstration against its source, then retype the unchanged source into three tools.
labels.redesign: When an output has a different job
labels.redesignBody: If the three tools serve different audiences or functions, keep those needs and redesign the workflow from one checked source. Generate or adapt only what each use requires. If the outputs are duplicates, remove the repeated typing.
labels.attemptIntro: Choose an activity you can examine comfortably. Separate two difficult parts. For each one, state the value it is claimed to serve, what the operation actually produces, and what you would retain, redesign or remove. Leave a connection unresolved when you do not have enough evidence.

labels.question: A project is important, so every tedious operation must be necessary.
labels.questionAnswer: Importance of the whole project does not establish the contribution of each operation. Trace what each one actually does.

operations.name: Check the demonstration against its source
operations.actualContribution: Comparison can reveal an incorrect or missing step before learners rely on it.
operations.decision: Retain the check, while keeping it proportionate to the risk and use.

operations.name: Retype the same unchanged source into three tools
operations.difficulty: Repeats manual entry and creates more chances for drift.
operations.claimedValue: The project is important, so all three copies must be prepared.
operations.actualContribution: When the copies have the same content and role, retyping adds no separate verification or learner-facing function.
operations.decision: Remove duplicate typing. If uses differ, redesign from one checked source and preserve only the needed adaptations.

assessment.guidedQuestion: Does a project's importance prove that every difficult operation is necessary?
assessment.learnerCheck: Can you trace a difficulty to what its operation actually contributes?
assessment.outcomeCheck: Does the revised activity preserve the valued result while removing or redesigning an unsupported cost?
assessment.changeAccount: If removing an operation damages the valued result, restore it or redesign the workflow to preserve its function.
